newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA '97 MAIZE ESTIMATE RISES, SUNFLOWER STEADY.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA '97 MAIZE ESTIMATE RISES, SUNFLOWER STEADY.

text.p: South Africa's National Crop Estimates Committee said on Monday it estimated the 1997 commercial maize crop at 7.966 million tonnes, up from its 7.660 million tonnes a month ago.
This is still sharply down on the 1996 crop of 9.694 million tonnes.
This year's crop was expected to comprise 4.333 million tonnes of white maize and 3.633 million tonnes of yellow, the committee said in its fifth official estimate for the new season.
Last year's maize crop comprised 5.836 million tonnes of white maize and 3.858 million tonnes of yellow.
The estimates committee's figures exclude maize grown in South Africa's former homeland areas which is mainly for subsistence use. This maize adds around 550,000 tonnes to the total estimate.
The fifth official sunflower seed estimate for 1997 forecast a crop of 450,000 tonnes, unchanged from last month. This is also well down on last year's 755,000 tonnes.
